open_items: ILO blanket-403 provider_down episode: ninth occurrence, started cycle 396, STILL OPEN at cycle 403 -- eight consecutive cycles unresolved (396-403), roughly 16 hours, confirmed with a live recheck at 2026-08-27T18:43:24Z still returning 403, and network sanity-checked against ECB and OECD direct (both 200) at the same moment to rule out the routine's own network. Priors: 244, 251, 260, 264, 272, 281, 321, 382, all but 321 resolved within a single cycle (321 took two cycles, gateway-data-only tail at 322). This occurrence is now well past every prior precedent and approaching the roughly 24h/12-cycle mark (cycle 407) previously set as the point to treat this as a standing block rather than a transient outage. All ILO contract assertions read `broken` (observed 403) at cycle 403, the same blanket condition surfacing through contracts, not a separate finding. ALERTED this run. Watch closely: if cycle 407 arrives without a healthy reading, treat it as a standing block and flag that the gateway's ILO request pattern (headers, rate) may need review.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: twenty-third and twenty-fourth episodes, cycles 401 and 403 (403 STILL OPEN at time of writing), each a one-cycle flap so far -- cycle 402 was clean healthy in between. Prior episode was cycle 397, resolved by 398, healthy through 399 and 400. Consistent with the long-running one-cycle-flap pattern (the gateway's own 60s call deadline firing under a slow response), not a new bug; live recheck at cycle 403 confirmed the direct path answers HTTP 200 in 28.4s, under the 60s deadline. ALERTED this run since status changed since last run's recorded state (was healthy at cycle 400). Standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result in monitor/checks_gateway.py) remains open as a code-change-scope fix, not actioned by this read-only routine.

ILO gateway_issue, both gateway metadata and gateway data HTTP 403 together, direct healthy: first occurrence of this exact combination, cycle 384, resolved by cycle 385. Distinct from the gateway-data-only flap (cycles 322, 370, metadata still passing) and from the gateway-metadata-500 episode (cycles 268-269, HTTP 500 not 403, data still passing). No second occurrence through cycle 403. Watch for a second occurrence of this specific shape.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: eleventh occurrence, cycle 381, resolved by cycle 382. All eleven occurrences have now resolved within one cycle. Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py).

ILO gateway-data-only 403 flap (standalone): two occurrences on record, cycle 370 (resolved by 371) and cycle 322 (tail end of the cycle 321 blanket-403 episode). Both resolved within one to two cycles. No new occurrence through cycle 403 (the cycle 384 and 396-403 episodes are the different both-metadata-and-data or blanket shapes, see above). Watch for a third occurrence of this standalone data-only shape.

Watch for a second occurrence; escalate if it recurs.
